q.en: What is Fluency actually measuring, according to this chapter?
q.bn: এই chapter অনুযায়ী, Fluency আসলে কী measure করে?

options.en: How fast you can speak
Pace and flow, not raw speed
options.bn: Pace এবং flow, raw speed না

options.en: How many words you use
How loudly you speak

why.en: Fluency is about a natural pace with few long pauses or restarts — not about speaking as fast as possible.
why.bn: Fluency একটা natural pace নিয়ে, খুব কম long pause বা restart সহ — যতটা সম্ভব তাড়াতাড়ি কথা বলা না।

options.en: Whether your ideas connect logically for the listener
options.bn: তোমার idea গুলো listener-এর জন্য logically connect করে কিনা

options.en: How many grammar rules you know
Your accent strength
How formal your vocabulary is

why.en: Coherence is about logical connection between ideas, often shown through appropriate linking words.
why.bn: Coherence idea-গুলোর মধ্যে logical connection নিয়ে, যা প্রায়ই appropriate linking word দিয়ে দেখানো হয়।

q.en: Is occasional use of "well," "actually," or "you know" harmful to your Fluency score?
q.bn: কখনো কখনো "well," "actually," বা "you know" ব্যবহার করা কি Fluency score-এর জন্য harmful?

options.en: Yes, any filler word is always penalised
options.bn: হ্যাঁ, কোনো filler word-ই সবসময় penalise হয়

options.en: No — used sparingly, they're normal thinking-time fillers
options.bn: না — sparingly ব্যবহার করলে, এগুলো normal thinking-time filler

options.en: Only in Part 3, never in Part 1
Only if said in Bangla

why.en: A little hesitation is normal even for native speakers — the real problem is frequent long pauses or constant sound-based fillers like repeated "umm."
why.bn: একটু hesitation native speaker-দের জন্যও normal — আসল সমস্যা frequent long pause বা বারবার "umm"-এর মতো sound-based filler।

q.en: Which of these sentences shows better Coherence, according to this chapter's example?
q.bn: এই chapter-এর example অনুযায়ী, নিচের কোন sentence-টা better Coherence দেখায়?

options.en: "I like my job. It's hard. I'm tired. I like the people."
options.bn: "I like my job. It's hard. I'm tired. I like the people."

options.en: "I like my job, even though it's quite demanding — I'm often tired by the end of the day, but I stick with it mainly because of the people I work with."
options.bn: "I like my job, even though it's quite demanding — I'm often tired by the end of the day, but I stick with it mainly because of the people I work with."

options.en: "Job. Hard. Tired. People. Good."
Both are equally coherent

why.en: The second version uses the same ideas but connects them logically with linking words, rather than listing disconnected short statements.
why.bn: দ্বিতীয় version একই idea ব্যবহার করে কিন্তু linking word দিয়ে logically connect করে, disconnected short statement-এর list না করে।

q.en: Is a brief self-correction mid-sentence (e.g. "I mean...") penalised in the Speaking test?
q.bn: মাঝ-sentence-এ একটা brief self-correction (যেমন "I mean...") কি Speaking test-এ penalise হয়?

options.en: Yes, any self-correction loses marks
No — a quick, natural self-correction is normal; repeated lengthy ones hurt Fluency
options.bn: না — একটা quick, natural self-correction normal; repeated lengthy self-correction Fluency-কে ক্ষতি করে

options.en: Only for Grammatical Range, never for Fluency
options.bn: শুধু Grammatical Range-এর জন্য, Fluency-এর জন্য কখনো না

options.en: Only if done in Part 2

why.en: Examiners don't expect 100% accuracy in live speech — a brief, natural self-correction is fine, but repeated lengthy self-correction derails fluency.
why.bn: Examiner-রা live speech-এ ১০০% accuracy আশা করে না — একটা brief, natural self-correction ঠিক আছে, কিন্তু repeated lengthy self-correction fluency-কে derail করে।
